question: Does the official publisher page for the Kodak Research multi-aperture study expose a complete, machine-readable primary table that can independently test P4BD's fixed aperture law?

search_context.selection_reason: Best directly accessible primary multi-aperture photographic-film table found after current-literature search; newer work did not expose comparable measured numerical tables.

source.title: Experimental Study of rms Granularity as a Function of Scanning-Spot Size
source.journal: Journal of the Optical Society of America
source.rights_scope: in-copyright publisher page; local internal research audit only; no redistribution

required_film_names: Eastman Fine Grain Release Positive Film

branch_rule.source_pass: Open one separately frozen fixed-law confirmation using exact table values and film-group separation.
branch_rule.source_fail: Close the source without PDF access, OCR, figure digitization, alternate mirrors or table repair.

forbidden: download the subscription PDF or bypass publisher access controls
redistribute publisher HTML or table content as a released dataset
fit an aperture exponent during source audit
treat historical B&W laboratory films as Kodak 250D or modern stock calibration
render photographs or alter product defaults
claim_ceiling: Internal source-feasibility evidence from one official in-copyright 1959 Kodak Research multi-aperture table; not modern stock, colour, process, scanner, microscopic geometry, NPS calibration or product evidence.
